text: The custody movement of rwb-comms is published as POST /notices/{noticeId}/custody-movements with the Movement answer and GET /notices/{noticeId}/custody-movements with the Movement list, under the base /api/recovery/comms/v1, with the seven-element Movement of the legacy custody row DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024 and the five required request fields documentId, movedAt, fromLocation, toLocation and heldBy.
why: No source names a custody operation, a request, an answer or a table for rwb-comms: the TSD P6 inventory holds eleven operations and none of them is a movement, and TSD P6 T3.1 holds four entities and no custody entity, so the elements that carry the feature are fixed by the contract baseline.
read: FSD P6 A2.19; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 and T3.1; legacy RWB-E4-040 Endpoints and Data
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-comms at the contract baseline review
impact: The two paths and the shapes are fixed for the app story to build against on Day 1; a change after sign-off needs a new major version.

text: The physical document and every custody row stay with P5 rwb-document, reached through the Ownership Map rows POST /documents/{documentId}/custody (API-P5-007) and the document read, declared as consumed shapes and faked, with no C dependency row because no P5 contract story is named for this key.
why: The legacy key held document and document_custody in the module's own schema, and the target ownership of both rows is the document hub, so this service declares no custody table and no cross-schema key (DP-01).
read: Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map rows recorded in RWB-P6-E4040-APP; Template and Rules §R5.4 and §R5.5 (DP-01, DP-11)
confirm: rwb-document owner and the solution architect at the baseline review
impact: The movement is recorded by its owner; this service keeps the notice reference and reads the history on the owner's contract, and the C row is added when the P5 contract story is planned.

text: The decision record of a movement is the local decision-record library's element written before the change on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, and the decision code, the rule id, the rule version, the eligible notice states, the location and holder vocabularies and the refusal texts are reference data or parameters read with the version in force, never constants of the contract.
why: DP-03 gives the record to the local library and BR-P6-019 and Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 forbid fixing in code or contract any value a business person may change, and no source gives the decision code or the rule id of a movement.
read: FSD P6 A2.19.3.1 (BR-P6-019, VR-P6-019-1); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-39; Template and Rules §R5.5 (DP-03) and §R7.2 s17
confirm: Decision-library owner and the configuration owner at the baseline review
impact: A new decision code, a new eligible state or a new location is a data row, not a release, and a movement whose record cannot be written does not proceed.

text: The one consumed event of this surface is rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1 (EV-05) on rwb.case.events.v1, owned by P3 and keyed by caseId, consumed inside rwb-comms with the inbox dedupe so a movement on a closed case or under legal hold is refused.
why: Architecture v5 slide 13 shows rwb-comms listening to rwb-case events, and R-UNI-20 stops every outbound action and automated decision on a case under legal hold, so the case state has to be known inside the service; no custody event exists in the catalogue for the reverse direction.
read: Architecture v5 slide 13 (P6 row) and slide 42 (event 05, 08); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-20; Template and Rules §R5.5 (DP-09)
confirm: rwb-case owner at the baseline review
impact: The service holds a case-state projection for the check and publishes nothing of its own; a second event would need a new row and a new fake.

text: Both movement operations declare the capability area Documents, with right C on the POST and right R on the GET, and their role lists are rwb-access data: RW-LEGAL holds Documents CRUA and RW-LITOFF holds Documents CRU in TSD P6 T6.1, so the legal counsel of the legacy story can perform both.
why: No source states the right of a custody operation, the legacy permission table names Litigation C and Litigation R for the two notice operations that belong to the notice feature, and the physical document is a Documents capability area object in TSD P6 T6.1.
read: TSD P6 v2 T6.1 and T6.2; legacy RWB-E4-040 Permission checks
confirm: Security architect and the rwb-access owner at the baseline review
impact: The document declares a capability area and a right per operation and holds no role code; a change of right is a data change, not a contract change.

text: The legacy screen SCR-33 Template approval belongs to the template feature and shows no custody movement; the movement is shown on the custody surface of rwb-document through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and that screen identifier is not named by any source read for this key.
why: The legacy story body describes a movement of an original while its own screen table names the template approval screen, and FSD P6 holds no custody screen, so a P6 screen cannot be claimed for the feature.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-040 Screen and states; FSD P6 screen list; Architecture v5 slide 10 notes; Template and Rules §R5.5 (DP-19)
confirm: Business analyst of P6 and the platform route owner
impact: No screen is built by this story; the baseline fixes only the answers the route merges and names SCR-33 as another feature's.
